experiment_description: A proof-of-principle ultra-compact weak-focusing electron storage ring is operated to test the central concept of three-dimensional spiral injection: an injected beam enters a solenoid-type storage magnet with a vertical pitch angle so that the solenoidal fringe field and a weak-focusing radial field guide the orbit in three dimensions, while a comparatively long pulsed kicker supplies small vertical kicks over many turns rather than requiring a single-turn nanosecond kicker. The electron beam is generated by a thermionic electron gun and chopper system with momentum p = 297 keV/c, kinetic energy 80 keV, and injected bunch width 100 ns. The transport line consists of three rotatable quadrupole magnets, one bending magnet, and a pair of steering magnets; it injects the beam into a 22 cm storage ring inside a storage magnet at a pitch angle of 0.7 rad relative to the horizontal X-Y plane. The storage magnet consists of main and auxiliary solenoidal coils operated with opposite polarities to keep the solenoidal field on the storage midplane Z = 0 cm at Bz = 8.77 mT while producing a weak-focusing field potential with field index of order 10^-2 in the storage region. A kicker coil system with inductance 1.3 microhenry is located at Z = ±15 cm and is driven, for the kicker-on condition, with a 45 A, 140 ns pulsed current to generate a radial field component configured to maintain downward steering during spiral injection. The beam revolution period in the compact ring is 4.7 ns. Beam storage is diagnosed destructively with a plastic scintillating-fiber probe inserted vertically from above into the storage region; the fiber is 1 mm in diameter and 20 cm long, read by a photomultiplier tube, and has an electron CSDA range of about 100 micrometre for 297 keV/c electrons in the scintillator material. For the representative storage test, the probe tip is positioned at the storage midplane so that the fiber covers Z = 0 cm to Z = 20 cm within the storage region. The SciFi-probe voltage waveform, a bottom plastic-scintillator beam-loss monitor waveform, and the kicker current waveform measured by a Rogowski coil are recorded for kicker-on and kicker-off conditions, with each waveform averaged over 1000 injected shots. The operational storage criterion is defined as a SciFi-probe signal exceeding 5 times sigma_noise for a duration of at least 1 microsecond, where sigma_noise is the rms fluctuation of the voltage in a pre-injection time window; this threshold corresponds to a time much longer than the injected pulse width and to many revolutions, and is intended to distinguish stored beam from transiently circulating or lost particles.

beam_storage_observed_with_kicker.description: Whether the SciFi-probe waveform satisfies the predefined storage criterion under the spiral-injection condition with the pulsed kicker activated.

beam_storage_observed_without_kicker.description: Whether the SciFi-probe waveform satisfies the predefined storage criterion under otherwise comparable injection conditions without the pulsed kicker.

stored_signal_persistence_lower_bound_us.description: Lower bound on the duration for which the SciFi-probe storage signal remains above the predefined noise threshold in the kicker-on condition.

transient_signal_duration_without_kicker.description: Approximate duration scale of the SciFi-probe signal in the kicker-off condition, used to characterize non-stored transient circulation relative to the injected bunch width.

experiment_description: The vertical distribution of the stored beam is measured to test whether the beam accumulated by the three-dimensional spiral injection method is governed by the intentionally applied weak-focusing field rather than by accidental trapping. The same 297 keV/c, 80 keV, 100 ns pulsed electron beam, 0.7 rad pitch-angle injection, 22 cm ultra-compact weak-focusing storage ring, Bz = 8.77 mT storage-plane solenoidal field, and 45 A, 140 ns kicker-pulse spiral-injection configuration are used. Four weak-focusing field configurations are generated by setting the main and auxiliary solenoid coil currents to (IMAIN, IAUX) = (8.70 A, 5.20 A), (8.82 A, 5.67 A), (9.20 A, 7.16 A), and (9.60 A, 8.72 A), with opposite current polarities in the actual magnet circuit. For each configuration, the radial magnetic-field component Br as a function of vertical coordinate Z is characterized in the storage region and used to determine the storable vertical range; finite-element calculations are performed with Opera for comparison, and Monte Carlo tracking includes the dominant injection-trajectory uncertainty. The stored-beam population is probed with the same vertically inserted plastic scintillating-fiber detector, 1 mm in diameter and 20 cm long, read out by a photomultiplier tube. A Z-scan is performed by inserting the probe from above in 5 mm steps; at each probe-tip position Z, measured from the storage midplane Z = 0 cm, a waveform averaged over 1000 injected shots is recorded. The measured dependent signal for the scan is the time-integrated SciFi-probe voltage ISignal = integral VSignal(t) dt, where VSignal(t) is the measured probe voltage and the integration window is t = 560 ns to 9000 ns after injection, beginning just after the end of the kicker pulse. The upper edge of the stored-beam distribution is defined as the probe-tip Z position where ISignal decreases to 5 percent of its maximum value for that field configuration. This spatially resolved scan covers the vertical storage aperture region accessible from above and uses the integrated signal to average over a wide range of vertical and radial betatron phases.

edge_point_cm_imain_8p70_iaux_5p20.description: Measured upper vertical edge position of the stored-beam distribution for the weak-focusing configuration with IMAIN = 8.70 A and IAUX = 5.20 A, using the 5 percent ISignal criterion.

storable_range_cm_imain_8p70_iaux_5p20.description: Measured storable vertical range associated with the weak-focusing magnetic-field configuration with IMAIN = 8.70 A and IAUX = 5.20 A.
